title: kv: coldspot sweeper + adaptive lease allocator to reduce fragmentation and spill spikes
author: Asha Kim
description:
Motivation:
The KV cache in our serving runtime shows periodic latency and spill spikes under mixed tenant workloads. Root cause analysis indicated two contributing issues: (1) long-lived small allocations from tenant-specific hottext create severe fragmentation in slab regions, and (2) the current immediate-spill policy causes synchronized paging during backpressure periods which amplifies tail latency.

Proposal / what this PR changes:
- Introduces a background 'coldspot sweeper' that periodically scans slab segments and consolidates candidate cold ranges with low access density into contiguous free regions. The sweeper is tenant-aware (respects per-tenant isolation limits) and runs with adaptive throttling to avoid interfering with foreground inference.
- Adds an 'adaptive lease allocator' layer: small allocations get short leases that can be reclaimed eagerly when memory pressure rises; longer leases are promoted based on access frequency. Leases are charged to tenant budgets so noisy tenants get bounded reclaim pressure.
- Replaces the immediate synchronous spill path with a staged spill policy: first attempt compaction (using the sweeper), then soft-spill to host-paged segments, and only as a last resort trigger remote spill. This stagged path reduces spikey I/O during transient pressure.
- Adds new runtime knobs: sweeper.interval_ms, sweeper.backoff_factor, lease.small_ms, lease.promotion_threshold, and tenant.reclaim_quota. All knobs are configurable via the runtime config and default to conservative values.

Benchmarks / results:
- Microbench (multi-tenant emulation, 96 clients, mixed size 128B-8KB keys): 95th-percentile token latency reduced by ~28% under sustained load compared to main.
- Spill frequency under synthetic tenant burst test dropped 4x; peak disk throughput during burst reduced by 63%.
- Memory fragmentation score (fragmentation_metric_v2) improved by 35% on average across runs.

Compatibility and deployment plan:
- Feature is behind runtime flags: kv.sweeper.enabled and kv.leases.enabled (both default ON in canary, OFF in global rollout).
- Default parameters tuned conservatively for Hosted. Dedicated tenants can tune per-customer via console.
- Rollout plan: canary (2 clusters) -> 10% -> 50% -> global; we will monitor fragmentation metrics, spill counts, and tail latency.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: linked in PR comments (ENG-3421)
- [x] Unit tests for allocator promotion/eviction logic
- [x] Integration bench harness updated (bench/kv/coldspot_runner)
- [x] Runtime config knobs and docs updated
- [x] Observability: added metrics kv.sweeper.* and kv.lease.*

Rollback and safety:
- All changes are guarded by flags and runtime-configurable. If regressions appear, we can disable kv.sweeper.enabled and kv.leases.enabled via the control plane and fall back to previous spill path. We added a non-destructive dry-run mode for the sweeper to validate candidate regions before compaction.

Related work:
- Builds on prior work in ENG-2990 (async compaction) and complements the pager coalescer changes from earlier quarters.

Notes: Description includes the design rationale and operational guidance — reviewers, please focus on the lease promotion invariants and tenant quota semantics.
